items.title: Tony Marino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 25, 2025
items.q: when we started with her she ended up getting Kenny Werner to do musical arrangements for her... We had synthesizer... drums... Well we played with Jamey Haddad... Jamey and I played with her

ctx.x: Was that a like a band? Was that a quartet or was that a larger thing?

Oh there was different, there was a lot of different – when we started with her she ended up getting Kenny Werner to do musical arrangements for her. So he would bring in some friends. We had synthesizer, we had violin, we had Billy Drewes on whatever horns he was playing you know could be flute, whatever, clarinet to alto, tenor you know, and guitar a couple of times they would use, drums, sometimes drums and percussion. Well we played with Jamey Haddad was a great drummer/percussionist you know. Jamey and I…

band opening up and you know, hitting hard. We were still playing a show for – but it was really beautiful stuff ‘cause Kenny had such a great command on harmony you know. It went into duos, man that was a mind-blower because he would just open up like turning on a faucet of the sink and he would throw everything out there you know. And she would be right on it. She would come right back and I mean I’d be lost sometimes, we’d take it so far out. But she nailed it. She was like right in every beat with her – with…
